newCandidatesThisWeek.rationale: YouTube Shorts 2026 has compressed the effective hook window to 2 seconds — before the existing edit_reels_two_second_hook (Instagram-tuned) and edit_three_signal_70pct_hook (3-second compound hook). This is a YouTube-specific 2-second stop-scroll template: visual-only promise in frame 0-2s with no title card, no intro, optimised for Shorts' vertical-swipe context. Distinct from Reels variant in pacing spec and metadata-match requirements unique to YouTube's Shorts algorithm.

Structured beat-every-1.5s editing cadence: punch-ins, b-roll inserts, and visual-cue timing enforced at 1.5–3 second intervals throughout the full clip to maintain retention beyond the hook. Not covered by edit_rapid_cut_pacing (which handles rapid montage) or edit_completion_rate_cut (which governs full-clip completion arc) — this tool specifically enforces the beat-timing grid as an edit template, making it usable as a standalone rhythm layer on any hunting clip regardless of narrative structure.

Structured narrative arc for hunting film clips: start-to-finish story structure (pre-hunt setup → field action → outcome reveal) with audience-retention checkpoints — matching the emerging demand from TikTok hunting creation courses. Distinct from edit_pov_field_camera (POV framing tool) and edit_reels_completion_arc (platform-completion-rate tool) because this governs the story skeleton of a full hunt sequence rather than a camera angle or completion metric. Fills gap for creators wanting CutPilot to auto-structure multi-clip hunt footage into a coherent narrative arc.

Flop-Core Instagram Reels template: structures a 'failure reveal' clip — missed shot, gear fail, or unexpected field moment — with specific caption framing ('I can't believe I…'), reaction cut structure, and original-audio-first edit spec that avoids copyrighted music restrictions on business accounts. Distinct from edit_reaction_reveal_cut (which handles product/information reveal reactions) because Flop-Core requires the failure event as the primary content unit, not a reaction overlay. A significant new Instagram format appearing in September 2026 tracked by multiple sources.

'10/10 Habits' rating-hook template: structures a short-form clip around a numeric rating reveal hook ('I give this [gear/tip/habit] a 10/10 because…') with a specific title-card spec for the rating number, a 2-second hold on the score before the reveal, and a CTA comment-prompt at the end ('What would you rate it?'). Not covered by existing hook tools — the numeric-rating reveal structure is a distinct hook mechanic that combines information-delivery with interactive comment-bait, both absent from current tools.

UGC-style field-condition product demo template: structures a hunting gear Reels demo with ambient field audio preserved, natural lighting treatment (no studio correction), affiliate-link caption spec, and a 3-beat reveal (problem → product → field test result). Distinct from edit_gear_check_reveal_sequence (TikTok flat-lay format with lower-third tags) because this is an Instagram-specific field-demo profile with UGC aesthetic intentionally preserved — no colour grade, raw sound — to match the authenticity signal driving Instagram algorithm reach in this niche.

LinkedIn-optimised 15–30 second cut profile: trims any source clip to the 15–30s sweet spot with LinkedIn's square/portrait crop, burned-in professional captions (no emoji, clean sans-serif), silent-autoplay-first audio mix, and a value-dense opening 3 seconds targeting professional buyers. Partially overlaps edit_reformat_for_linkedin (which handles format/crop conversion) but adds the duration-enforcement constraint and the professional-buyer edit posture (cut for attention efficiency, not entertainment pacing) as a distinct export spec for B2B outdoor brands.
